narrativeBlocks.title: A strength that can be found
narrativeBlocks.body: In one tale Ralston records, Koschei locates his death outside his body: inside an egg, inside a duck, inside a hare, inside a casket beneath an oak.

narrativeBlocks.title: The nested hiding place
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Ralston's English text; whitespace normalized): “There stands an oak, and under the oak is a casket, and in the casket is a hare, and in the hare is a duck, and in the duck is an egg, and”

narrativeBlocks.title: A choice on the journey
narrativeBlocks.body: On his search, Ivan considers killing a young wolf. Its mother asks him to spare the cub and promises a good turn; Ivan lets it live.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not flatten variants
narrativeBlocks.body: Ralston compares multiple reported versions of Koschei. The external death motif appears in a tale he quotes; details vary and do not define every Slavic story.

narrativeBlocks.title: Discovery changes the contest
narrativeBlocks.body: The story makes knowledge of a hidden vulnerability more important than a direct contest of strength.
